text:
Can you help me write the project summary for a grant application? I'm the managing attorney at a two-lawyer legal aid clinic that represents tenants facing eviction. We're applying to our state bar foundation for $90,000 to hire a third attorney for two years.

Facts:
- Last year 1,140 eviction cases were filed in our county. We represented the tenant in 163 of them.
- In the cases where we represented the tenant, 58% ended with the tenant staying in the home or getting at least 60 days to move. We don't have a comparable number for tenants without a lawyer.
- We turned away about 300 tenants last year because no attorney was free.
- Our two attorneys each carry about 80 open cases. One of them is leaving in June.
- A third attorney would cost $78,000 a year with benefits. The foundation's maximum award is $45,000 a year.
- The county gives us $60,000 a year, and that contract is up for renewal in October.

The project summary has to be 300 words or less.

Yes. Before I draft, I have a few questions. Your answers would change what the summary says, and I'd rather not guess:

1. **Where will the other $33,000 a year come from?** The attorney costs $78,000 a year and the foundation caps awards at $45,000. Reviewers will spot that gap right away. Is part of the county's $60,000 going to cover it, or another funder, or reserves? And is that money committed or still pending?

2. **Has the county contract been renewed?** If the October you mentioned was last month, what happened? If it's October 2027, how confident are you that it will be renewed? That tells me whether to present county funding as stable or leave it out of the match.

3. **When the attorney leaves in June, will you rehire for that spot from other funds?** If not, this grant would really keep you at two attorneys, not take you to three. That's a different case to make, and the foundation will want it stated honestly. Which is it?

4. **How many cases does one attorney close in a year?** "About 80 open at a time" doesn't tell me that. With a yearly figure I can say how many more tenants a third attorney would serve, for example "roughly X of the 300 we now turn away." If you don't have it, I'll leave the projection out instead of estimating.

5. **Does the foundation give guidelines for the summary?** For example, required sections or scoring criteria. And what are the clinic's name and county?

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write around them.

1. A family fund has pledged $20,000 a year for two years toward the new attorney. The rest comes from our general budget. None of the county money goes to it.

2. It hasn't come up for renewal yet; that's this coming October. I can't promise the county will renew it.

3. I don't know yet whether we'll rehire for her spot from other funds. She has agreed to spend her last month training the new hire.

4. I don't know. Leave the projection out.

5. I don't know of any guidelines beyond the 300-word limit. We're the Tenant Defense Project.

Here's the summary. It runs about 250 words.

<final_document>
**Project Summary — Tenant Defense Project**

Last year, 1,140 eviction cases were filed in [County]. The Tenant Defense Project represented the tenant in 163 of them. In 58% of those cases, the tenant stayed in the home or got at least 60 days to move. We turned away about 300 other tenants because no attorney was free to take their case.

Our two attorneys each carry about 80 open cases, which leaves no room for more. In June, one of them is leaving.

We request $90,000 over two years ($45,000 a year) to hire an eviction defense attorney. The position costs $78,000 a year with benefits. A family fund has pledged $20,000 a year for both years, and we will pay the remaining $13,000 a year from our general budget. The position does not depend on our $60,000 county contract, which comes up for renewal in October 2027.

The new attorney will start before our departing attorney leaves. She has agreed to spend her last month training the new hire, so her cases can pass to the new attorney without a gap in representation.

Without a new hire, we will have one attorney after June. With this grant, we will keep at least two full-time attorneys defending tenants in [County] for the next two years. If we also fill the departing attorney's position, the new hire will be our third attorney, and we can begin taking cases from the tenants we now turn away.
</final_document>

A few things to check:

- **Third attorney or replacement:** You don't yet know if you'll rehire for the departing attorney's spot. So the summary says plainly that the grant at least keeps you at two attorneys, and makes three possible. Reviewers will likely work out the staffing math either way. Saying it up front protects your credibility. Once you know you'll rehire, change the last paragraph to say the grant creates a third position.
- **The 58% figure:** I left it as your result and didn't compare it to tenants without a lawyer, since you don't have that number. If you find county or court data on unrepresented tenants, adding it would make the summary much stronger.
- **Placeholders and dates:** Replace [County] with your county's name. I wrote "October 2027" for the county renewal and assumed the June departure is June 2027. Correct either one if I've got it wrong.
